info.title: tt-scrap
info.description:
Authenticated extraction, download, and direct Telegram-delivery API for TikTok and
Instagram.

## Client integration

Use the origin that served this document as the API base URL. Every `/v1/*` request
requires `Authorization: Bearer <TT_SCRAP_API_KEY>`. `/openapi.json`, `/docs`, and
health endpoints are public. API errors use `ErrorResponse`; keep `error.request_id`
for diagnostics and branch on the stable `error.code` rather than message text.
Every response also includes `X-Request-ID` and `Server-Timing: app;dur=<milliseconds>`;
send a caller-generated `X-Request-ID` to correlate the response with server logs.

### TikTok information and downloads

Call `resolveTikTokUrl` to turn a short share URL into its full TikTok post URL and
numeric `source_id` without extracting metadata or downloading media. This lets a
client check its own database before doing any extraction work.

Call `extractTikTok` with a public TikTok URL. The response contains metadata and
opaque `AssetDescriptor.download_url` paths instead of upstream CDN URLs. Resolve a
relative download path against the tt-scrap base URL, send the bearer token again,
and consume it before `expires_at`. TikTok metadata and `extraction_id` are cached
briefly (60 seconds by default); asset tokens normally live longer. A repeated URL
within the metadata TTL reuses extraction work unless `refresh=true`.

TikTok uses the Android app API. Video selection uses API metadata only: highest
pixel resolution, then frame rate, then bitrate, with no CDN quality probes.
Videos include their audio; downloads and Telegram delivery preserve the selected
file without re-encoding.

Call `extractInstagram` with a post or reel URL to receive ordered image/video items,
opaque asset paths, and available cover, dimensions, duration, engagement, music and
caption metadata. The Android app method is the default; the server can configure
the previous provider as `legacy` or as fallback. `method` identifies the successful
method, and `source_id` remains the shortcode. Download media[].asset.download_url
with the API bearer token before expires_at. Its `extraction_id` can be passed
directly to `deliverInstagramToTelegram` while cached, avoiding another Instagram
API request.

### Direct Telegram delivery

Call `deliverTikTokToTelegram` or `deliverInstagramToTelegram`; the Telegram bot token
is configured on tt-scrap and must not be sent by the client. TikTok `source` accepts
exactly one of `url`, a recent `extraction_id`, or `video_id`; `video_id` is valid only
with `delivery="audio"`. Instagram `source` accepts exactly one of `url` or a recent
`extraction_id`. `refresh=true` cannot be combined with `extraction_id`.

Delivery modes:

* `media`: video via `sendVideo`; one slideshow image via `sendPhoto`; multiple
  slideshow images via one or more `sendMediaGroup` calls.
* `document`: video via `sendDocument`; slideshow images as document media groups.
  Original image bytes are preserved, except that WebP images are sent as full-size
  JPEG because Telegram rejects WebP documents in media groups. Video/photo technical
  metadata is omitted.
* `audio`: TikTok music via `sendAudio`, with inferred title, performer, duration,
  filename, and a converted thumbnail when available.

Instagram supports `media` and `document`. A mixed carousel is sent in source order
as photo/video media groups; document mode sends every carousel item as a document.

`telegram.chat_id` is required. Other Telegram fields are optional overrides. The
client must not provide managed multipart fields: `video`, `audio`, `photo`,
`document`, `media`, `thumbnail`, or `cover`. Parameter validity depends on the
chosen media and delivery mode; unsupported combinations return
`telegram_parameter_not_supported`. A one-image TikTok slideshow accepts a caption
on its single photo or document; multi-image TikTok slideshows do not accept caption
fields. Instagram carousel captions are attached to the first item of the first album
batch.

For one Telegram API call, tt-scrap returns Telegram's JSON and HTTP status directly,
with X-Telegram-Method identifying the actual Telegram method.
For several album batches, it returns `TelegramMultiDeliveryResponse` in order. HTTP
207 means at least one earlier batch succeeded before a later failure. Do not
automatically retry an ambiguous delivery timeout or an entire partial delivery,
because doing so can duplicate Telegram messages.

### Slideshows and images

TikTok slideshows and Instagram carousels are prepared fully before the first
Telegram call, retain their original order, and are partitioned into valid albums of
2-10 items. Static JPEG, PNG, and WebP pass through byte-for-byte. Only HEIC/HEIF
photos are converted asynchronously to baseline JPEG; other unsupported formats are
rejected before upload. Document mode preserves original image formats, except WebP, which is converted to
full-size JPEG. Video and
audio covers are normalized to Telegram-compatible JPEG thumbnails when possible.

get.description: Report whether the process can serve HTTP requests.
Checks TikTok identity readiness and the configured Instagram backend. App sessions do not require RAPIDAPI_KEY; the legacy method and legacy fallback require that key.

503.description: A required service credential is not configured

post.description:
Follow a TikTok share link and return its full post URL and numeric ID.
Share links on `tiktok.com` subdomains and `tt.site` are accepted.

This endpoint performs redirect resolution only. It does not call the TikTok
metadata extractor, create asset references, or download any media.

post.description:
Resolve, prepare, and upload TikTok media using the server's Telegram bot.

`media` sends videos with metadata or slideshows as photo galleries;
`document` sends original/file media without Telegram technical metadata; and
`audio` sends the post's music. The caller supplies destination and optional
Telegram parameters, but never multipart media fields or a bot token.

A single Telegram call is returned byte-for-byte with Telegram's HTTP status.
Multiple gallery batches use `TelegramMultiDeliveryResponse`; HTTP 207 means an
earlier batch succeeded before a later one failed. Do not blindly retry the
whole request after timeouts or ambiguous upload failures because that can
duplicate messages.

401.description: Missing or invalid tt-scrap bearer token

default.description: A raw Telegram Bot API failure or a stable tt-scrap error envelope. Do not automatically retry an ambiguous upload response.

207.description: Some earlier Telegram album batches succeeded before a failure

post.description: Fetch Instagram metadata without downloading CDN media. Returns ordered opaque media and thumbnail references, cover, dimensions, duration, engagement counts, music and caption when available. Download each media[].asset.download_url with the API bearer token before expires_at. The server selects the app or legacy method and optional fallback; method records which succeeded. source_id remains the post shortcode (or a legacy story media ID).

401.description: Missing or invalid tt-scrap bearer token

default.description: Stable tt-scrap error envelope; inspect error.code

post.description:
Resolve, prepare, and upload Instagram media using the server's Telegram bot.

A single image uses `sendPhoto`, a single video uses `sendVideo`, and a carousel
uses mixed `sendMediaGroup` batches. Document mode sends all items as files.
In media mode, static JPEG, PNG, and WebP images pass through unchanged. HEIC/HEIF images and
usable video thumbnails are converted asynchronously; other image formats are
rejected in media mode.

One Telegram call is returned verbatim. Multiple batches return
`TelegramMultiDeliveryResponse`; do not retry an ambiguous or partial upload
automatically because that can duplicate messages.

default.description: A raw Telegram Bot API failure or a stable tt-scrap error envelope. Do not automatically retry an ambiguous upload response.

207.description: Some earlier Telegram album batches succeeded before a failure

get.description:
Download an opaque asset URL returned by an extraction response.

Send the same tt-scrap bearer token used for extraction. The token is temporary;
download before the descriptor's `expires_at`. TikTok videos include their audio
and are returned without re-encoding.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename with a detected-format extension

get.description: Read preparation progress from RAM. No registration is started.

post.description: Start or reuse a background job that registers devices for ten identity slots per proxy address. Signing seeds are not fetched; requests fetch them on demand. Each proxy has one worker, with a minimum ten-second gap after each attempt completes. Repeated requests reuse an active job. Accepts no body or an empty JSON object. Startup runs this job before opening the API listener.

Validate a batch, choose least-assigned proxy routes, check egress, login with optional TOTP, verify each session and persist successful accounts. Accepts the G2G CSV format: User ID / Email Address, Password, First Secret Question (TOTP). At most 100 accounts / 1 MiB. Synchronous, sequential processing; successful rows survive subsequent failures. A login rate limit skips remaining rows. HTTP 200 contains per-row results, not a guarantee of successful login. Unchanged imports return duplicate. Verified replacement sessions can reactivate dead accounts; login-only updates preserve dead status. Supplied username/password/TOTP credentials are retained privately for automatic session recovery; re-importing changed login credentials for a known account returns updated and keeps its working session and route. Cookie imports for known accounts are verified on the saved proxy and device, then replace the active session while preserving the login backup. A known username is sufficient to add password/TOTP to a cookie-only account; cookies need not be sent again. Login aliases are matched by verified user ID. Failed verification changes nothing. Imports are available even while Instagram readiness is false. New accounts select a device profile once (random by default); the generated device IDs and profile persist with the session. Unknown profiles reject the entire batch before contacting Instagram. CSV accepts an optional Cookies column containing a JSON cookie array. Browser-cookie imports accept one JSON cookie array per account (text/plain or multipart file), a single array as application/json, or accounts entries with cookies. Cookie entries require Instagram sessionid and ds_user_id cookies and may also include username/password/TOTP. Cookies are preferred; expired or explicitly rejected sessions fall back to the supplied login credentials. Network errors, rate limits and challenges do not trigger password fallback. Cookies are verified on the selected route, saved as JSON, and used to derive Android authorization in memory only.

schema.description: UTF-8 CSV, optional BOM; First Secret Question contains the TOTP seed.
Browser export: one JSON array of cookie objects per account, separated by newlines. A single pretty-printed array is also accepted.

get.description: List active, reserve and dead accounts in oldest-first order. Session tokens and proxy credentials are never exposed. Active set size is configured with INSTAGRAM_ACTIVE_ACCOUNTS (default 10).

Static client profiles for account import. All use the Instagram Android TLS configuration with fresh handshake keys. This endpoint contains no account-specific IDs or secrets and is available before any account is loaded.

InstagramExtractionResponse.description: Normalized Instagram metadata and ordered temporary asset references. The app method supplies richer metadata; unavailable values, including values missing from the legacy provider, are null. Account credentials, proxy assignments, and upstream CDN URLs are never exposed.

media_type.description: Telegram media type selected for this item

thumbnail.description: Optional video thumbnail prepared for Telegram media mode

InstagramTelegramDeliveryRequest.title: InstagramTelegramDeliveryRequest
InstagramTelegramDeliveryRequest.description:
Request direct Telegram delivery of an Instagram post.

`media` sends photos, videos, or mixed media groups. `document` sends every
item as a file and preserves original image bytes, except WebP images, which are
sent as full-size JPEG. The Telegram bot token is
configured on tt-scrap and is not part of this request.

extraction_id.title: Extraction Id
extraction_id.description: Recent Instagram extraction_id; avoids another upstream request

InstagramTelegramSource.title: InstagramTelegramSource
InstagramTelegramSource.description: Exactly one Instagram source selector for Telegram delivery.

TelegramAPIResponse.description: Raw response envelope returned by the Telegram Bot API.

TelegramDeliveryRecord.title: TelegramDeliveryRecord
TelegramDeliveryRecord.description: One attempted Telegram album batch in delivery order.

TelegramMultiDeliveryResponse.title: TelegramMultiDeliveryResponse
TelegramMultiDeliveryResponse.description: Result used when a slideshow requires multiple Telegram album calls.

chat_id.description: Target chat ID or @channelusername accepted by the configured bot

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: Caption for single calls; Instagram carousels use the first item; multi-image TikTok slideshows reject it

TelegramParameters.title: TelegramParameters
TelegramParameters.description:
Destination and caller-controlled Telegram Bot API parameters.

Extra Telegram fields are forwarded when compatible with the selected method.
tt-scrap owns all multipart media fields, so callers must not supply `video`,
`audio`, `photo`, `document`, `media`, `thumbnail`, or `cover`. Fields supported
by one Telegram method can be rejected for another delivery/media combination.

TikTokTelegramDeliveryRequest.title: TikTokTelegramDeliveryRequest
TikTokTelegramDeliveryRequest.description:
Request server-side TikTok preparation and direct Telegram upload.

The Telegram bot token is server configuration, not part of this request.
`refresh` cannot be used with `source.extraction_id`.

url.title: Url
url.description: TikTok or tt.site share URL to resolve and extract

extraction_id.title: Extraction Id
extraction_id.description: Recent extraction_id; avoids URL resolution and extraction

video_id.title: Video Id
video_id.description: Numeric TikTok post ID; only valid when delivery is audio

TikTokTelegramSource.title: TikTokTelegramSource
TikTokTelegramSource.description:
Exactly one source selector for Telegram delivery.

`url` performs or reuses extraction, `extraction_id` reuses recent extraction
context, and `video_id` is accepted only for audio delivery.

audio.description: Instagram music downloads are not supported.

InstagramMusicMetadata.title: InstagramMusicMetadata
InstagramMusicMetadata.description: Music metadata supplied by Instagram, with a cover reference when available. Audio is always null; Instagram music downloads are not supported.

password.description: Retained privately for automatic password/TOTP recovery when the session expires.

totp_secret.description: Base32 TOTP secret or otpauth://totp URI. CSV uses First Secret Question.

device_profile.description: Optional profile ID from GET /v1/instagram/device-profiles. Omitted, empty or random selects a profile once for the new account. CSV accepts an optional Device Profile column.

row.description: One-based data row; excludes CSV header.

device_profile.description: Persisted device profile ID. Pre-profile sessions retain pixel-7-android-17.

accounts.description: Oldest first by database insertion order. Active accounts may temporarily be cooling down or busy.

InstagramCookieArray.description: Original Instagram browser cookies, including domain/path, hostOnly, secure, session and expirationDate attributes. Requires sessionid and ds_user_id applicable to i.instagram.com/api/v1/accounts/current_user/. Browser metadata is preserved. Expired cookies require complete username/password fallback credentials.
